What to look for

Leafy gall
A tight mass of small, distorted shoots at the crown or soil line.
Normal growth
Separate shoots growing their own stems and leaves, even when there are several.
Crown gall
A solid, irregular swelling rather than a cluster of shoots.
  • Photo checks stay on your device. Uploading for a human review is optional.
  • Experimental, not a diagnosis. It can be wrong, and often can’t decide.

A closer look. On your device.

Choose a clear photo, then tap Inspect photo. A small vision model runs in your browser and compares your photo against a source-checked set of published reference photos.

On-device checks. Optional private review.

The automatic checker runs on your device without an analysis API. Your photo is uploaded only if you choose “Send a photo for review” and confirm the form. Review photos, your email and notes are stored privately in Railway and sent to our review inbox through Resend so we can reply. Embedded photo metadata is removed before storage. Nothing is posted to GitHub.

Helping improve the checker

Training permission is optional and unchecked by default. With your permission, a reviewed photo may be used for reference matching, training and evaluation. Your email is never part of a training export. Submitting does not automatically add a photo to the model or confirm a diagnosis. Reply to our review email if you want to request deletion or withdraw permission.

A visual match isn’t a diagnosis.

This is an experimental comparison using a general-purpose model and 30 reference photos. These source labels have not been independently confirmed by this project. It has not been validated for diagnosing leafy gall. The result may be wrong, and “normal growth” does not rule out disease. A plant diagnostic clinic can advise on confirmation.

Anonymous usage analytics

We use PostHog to count visits, traffic sources, reference views and checker outcomes. Analytics uses no cookies or persistent visitor profiles. We do not send your photo, file name or image features, and session recording is disabled. We respect Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control.

For the most useful photo

Use daylight, keep the crown centred, and show the shoots and any unusual growth clearly. A distant flower photo won’t help.

An independent guide. These organisations are not affiliated with this website.

  • Oregon State University Plant Clinic ↗

Reference photographs

Leafy gall: Wild Horse Gardens and their disease biology guide. Normal growth: UC ANR. Crown gall: Dahlia Doctor. Photos belong to their respective owners.

The reference set

30 published visual examples: 12 leafy-gall appearances, 13 normal-growth appearances, and 5 crown-gall appearances. Labels follow their sources; they are not laboratory confirmations. View the source catalog ↗. Additional normal examples come from Idlewild Blooms and Summer Dreams Farm.

On-device checker

MobileCLIP-S0 with Transformers.js. Model and runtime are served by this site. The checker retrieves similar reference photos; it is not trained or validated as a disease classifier.
